title: Stephen's speech: the history of Israel + his martyrdom by stoning

paragraphs.text: And the high priest said, Are these things so?
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de ho archiereus· Ei tauta houtōs echei;

paragraphs.text: And he said, Brethren and fathers, hearken: The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran,
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε· Ὁ θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν,
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē· Andres adelphoi kai pateres, akousate· Ho theos tēs doxēs ōphthē tō patri hēmōn Abraam onti en tē Mesopotamia prin ē katoikēsai auton en Charran,

paragraphs.text: and said unto him, Get thee out of thy land, and from thy kindred, and come into the land which I shall show thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen pros auton· Exelthe ek tēs gēs sou kai ek tēs syngeneias sou, kai deuro eis tēn gēn hēn an soi deixō.

paragraphs.text: Then came he out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and dwelt in Haran: and from thence, when his father was dead, [God] removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell:
paragraphs.original: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν. κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε,
paragraphs.translit: tote exelthōn ek gēs Chaldaiōn katōkēsen en Charran. kakeithen meta to apothanein ton patera autou metōkisen auton eis tēn gēn tautēn eis hēn hymeis nyn katoikeite,

paragraphs.text: and he gave him none inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on: and he promised that he would give it to him in possession, and to his seed after him, when [as yet] he had no child.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk edōken autō klēronomian en autē oude bēma podos, kai epēngeilato dounai autō eis kataschesin autēn kai tō spermati autou metʼ auton, ouk ontos autō teknou.

paragraphs.text: And God spake on this wise, that his seed should sojourn in a strange land, and that they should bring them into bondage, and treat them ill, four hundred years.
paragraphs.original: ἐλάλησεν δὲ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·
paragraphs.translit: elalēsen de houtōs ho theos hoti estai to sperma autou paroikon en gē allotria, kai doulōsousin auto kai kakōsousin etē tetrakosia·

paragraphs.text: And the nation to which they shall be in bondage will I judge, said God: and after that shall they come forth, and serve me in this place.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ὁ θεὸς εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai to ethnos hō ean douleusousin krinō egō, ho theos eipen, kai meta tauta exeleusontai kai latreusousin moi en tō topō toutō.

paragraphs.text: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so [Abraham] begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac [begat] Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.
paragraphs.translit: kai edōken autō diathēkēn peritomēs· kai houtōs egennēsen ton Isaak kai perietemen auton tē hēmera tē ogdoē, kai Isaak ton Iakōb, kai Iakōb tous dōdeka patriarchas.

paragraphs.text: And the patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Joseph, sold him into Egypt: and God was with him,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Kai hoi patriarchai zēlōsantes ton Iōsēph apedonto eis Aigypton· kai ēn ho theos metʼ autou,

paragraphs.text: and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai exeilato auton ek pasōn tōn thlipseōn autou, kai edōken autō charin kai sophian enantion Pharaō basileōs Aigyptou, kai katestēsen auton hēgoumenon epʼ Aigypton kai holon ton oikon autou.

paragraphs.text: Now there came a famine over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance.
paragraphs.original: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: ēlthen de limos ephʼ holēn tēn Aigypton kai Chanaan kai thlipsis megalē, kai ouch hēuriskon chortasmata hoi pateres hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent forth our fathers the first time.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·
paragraphs.translit: akousas de Iakōb onta sitia eis Aigypton exapesteilen tous pateras hēmōn prōton·

paragraphs.text: And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph`s race became manifest unto Pharaoh.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ γένος Ἰωσήφ.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tō deuterō anegnōristhē Iōsēph tois adelphois autou, kai phaneron egeneto tō Pharaō to genos Iōsēph.

paragraphs.text: And Joseph sent, and called to him Jacob his father, and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.
paragraphs.original: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε,
paragraphs.translit: aposteilas de Iōsēph metekalesato Iakōb ton patera autou kai pasan tēn syngeneian en psychais hebdomēkonta pente,

paragraphs.text: And Jacob went down into Egypt; and he died, himself and our fathers;
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατέβη Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον. καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: kai katebē Iakōb eis Aigypton. kai eteleutēsen autos kai hoi pateres hēmōn,

paragraphs.text: and they were carried over unto Shechem, and laid in the tomb that Abraham bought for a price in silver of the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ἐν Συχέμ.
paragraphs.translit: kai metetethēsan eis Sychem kai etethēsan en tō mnēmati hō ōnēsato Abraam timēs argyriou para tōn hyiōn Hemmōr en Sychem.

paragraphs.text: But as the time of the promise drew nigh which God vouchsafed unto Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
paragraphs.original: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ὡμολόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ,
paragraphs.translit: Kathōs de ēngizen ho chronos tēs epangelias hēs hōmologēsen ho theos tō Abraam, ēuxēsen ho laos kai eplēthynthē en Aigyptō,

paragraphs.text: till there arose another king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph.
paragraphs.original: ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ.
paragraphs.translit: achri hou anestē basileus heteros epʼ Aigypton, hos ouk ēdei ton Iōsēph.

paragraphs.text: The same dealt craftily with our race, and ill-treated our fathers, that they should cast out their babes to the end they might not live.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς πατέρας τοῦ ποιεῖν τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζῳογονεῖσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: houtos katasophisamenos to genos hēmōn ekakōsen tous pateras tou poiein ta brephē ektheta autōn eis to mē zōogoneisthai.

paragraphs.text: At which season Moses was born, and was exceeding fair; and he was nourished three months in his father`s house.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς, καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ θεῷ· ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός·
paragraphs.translit: en hō kairō egennēthē Mōysēs, kai ēn asteios tō theō· hos anetraphē mēnas treis en tō oikō tou patros·

paragraphs.text: and when he was cast out, Pharaoh`s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.
paragraphs.original: ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν.
paragraphs.translit: ektethentos de autou aneilato auton hē thygatēr Pharaō kai anethrepsato auton heautē eis hyion.

paragraphs.text: And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians; and he was mighty in his words and works.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη Μωϋσῆς πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων, ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai epaideuthē Mōysēs pasē sophia Aigyptiōn, ēn de dynatos en logois kai ergois autou.

paragraphs.text: But when he was well-nigh forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταετὴς χρόνος, ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de eplērouto autō tesserakontaetēs chronos, anebē epi tēn kardian autou episkepsasthai tous adelphous autou tous hyious Israēl.

paragraphs.text: And seeing one [of them] suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, smiting the Egyptian:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn tina adikoumenon ēmynato kai epoiēsen ekdikēsin tō kataponoumenō pataxas ton Aigyption.

paragraphs.text: and he supposed that his brethren understood that God by his hand was giving them deliverance; but they understood not.
paragraphs.original: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν.
paragraphs.translit: enomizen de synienai tous adelphous hoti ho theos dia cheiros autou didōsin sōtērian autois, hoi de ou synēkan.

paragraphs.text: And the day following he appeared unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?
paragraphs.original: τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις καὶ συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών· Ἄνδρες, ἀδελφοί ἐστε· ἱνατί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους;
paragraphs.translit: tē te epiousē hēmera ōphthē autois machomenois kai synēllassen autous eis eirēnēn eipōn· Andres, adelphoi este· hinati adikeite allēlous;

paragraphs.text: But he that did his neighbor wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφʼ ἡμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: ho de adikōn ton plēsion apōsato auton eipōn· Tis se katestēsen archonta kai dikastēn ephʼ hēmōn;

paragraphs.text: Wouldest thou kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian yesterday?
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον;
paragraphs.translit: mē anelein me sy theleis hon tropon aneiles echthes ton Aigyption;

paragraphs.text: And Moses fled at this saying, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he begat two sons.
paragraphs.original: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ, οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο.
paragraphs.translit: ephygen de Mōysēs en tō logō toutō, kai egeneto paroikos en gē Madiam, hou egennēsen hyious dyo.

paragraphs.text: And when forty years were fulfilled, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου·
paragraphs.translit: Kai plērōthentōn etōn tesserakonta ōphthē autō en tē erēmō tou orous Sina angelos en phlogi pyros batou·

paragraphs.text: And when Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold, there came a voice of the Lord,
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν τὸ ὅραμα. προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ κυρίου·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Mōysēs idōn ethaumasen to horama. proserchomenou de autou katanoēsai egeneto phōnē kyriou·

paragraphs.text: I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob. And Moses trembled, and durst not behold.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ. ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Egō ho theos tōn paterōn sou, ho theos Abraam kai Isaak kai Iakōb. entromos de genomenos Mōysēs ouk etolma katanoēsai.

paragraphs.text: And the Lord said unto him, Loose the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος· Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου, ὁ γὰρ τόπος ἐφʼ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autō ho kyrios· Lyson to hypodēma tōn podōn sou, ho gar topos ephʼ hō hestēkas gē hagia estin.

paragraphs.text: I have surely seen the affliction of my people that is in Egypt, and have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them: and now come, I will send thee into Egypt.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα, καὶ κατέβην ἐξελέσθαι αὐτούς· καὶ νῦν δεῦρο ἀποστείλω σε εἰς Αἴγυπτον.
paragraphs.translit: idōn eidon tēn kakōsin tou laou mou tou en Aigyptō, kai tou stenagmou autou ēkousa, kai katebēn exelesthai autous· kai nyn deuro aposteilō se eis Aigypton.

paragraphs.text: This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? him hath God sent [to be] both a ruler and a deliverer with the hand of the angel that appeared to him in the bush.
paragraphs.original: Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν, ὃν ἠρνήσαντο εἰπόντες· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστήν, τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἄρχοντα καὶ λυτρωτὴν ἀπέσταλκεν σὺν χειρὶ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ὀφθέντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ βάτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Touton ton Mōysēn, hon ērnēsanto eipontes· Tis se katestēsen archonta kai dikastēn, touton ho theos kai archonta kai lytrōtēn apestalken syn cheiri angelou tou ophthentos autō en tē batō.

paragraphs.text: This man led them forth, having wrought wonders and signs in Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness forty years.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: houtos exēgagen autous poiēsas terata kai sēmeia en gē Aigyptō kai en Erythra Thalassē kai en tē erēmō etē tesserakonta.

paragraphs.text: This is that Moses, who said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall God raise up unto you from among your brethren, like unto me.
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ὁ εἴπας τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ.
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin ho Mōysēs ho eipas tois hyiois Israēl· Prophētēn hymin anastēsei ho theos ek tōn adelphōn hymōn hōs eme.

paragraphs.text: This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spake to him in the Mount Sinai, and with our fathers: who received living oracles to give unto us:
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ καὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ὃς ἐδέξατο λόγια ζῶντα δοῦναι ἡμῖν,
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin ho genomenos en tē ekklēsia en tē erēmō meta tou angelou tou lalountos autō en tō orei Sina kai tōn paterōn hēmōn, hos edexato logia zōnta dounai hēmin,

paragraphs.text: to whom our fathers would not be obedient, but thrust him from them, and turned back in their hearts unto Egypt,
paragraphs.original: ᾧ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἀπώσαντο καὶ ἐστράφησαν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν εἰς Αἴγυπτον,
paragraphs.translit: hō ouk ēthelēsan hypēkooi genesthai hoi pateres hēmōn, alla apōsanto kai estraphēsan en tais kardiais autōn eis Aigypton,

paragraphs.text: saying unto Aaron, Make us gods that shall go before us: for as for this Moses, who led us forth out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.
paragraphs.original: εἰπόντες τῷ Ἀαρών· Ποίησον ἡμῖν θεοὺς οἳ προπορεύσονται ἡμῶν· ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος, ὃς ἐξήγαγεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ἐγένετο αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: eipontes tō Aarōn· Poiēson hēmin theous hoi proporeusontai hēmōn· ho gar Mōysēs houtos, hos exēgagen hēmas ek gēs Aigyptou, ouk oidamen ti egeneto autō.

paragraphs.text: And they made a calf in those days, and brought a sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμοσχοποίησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ ἀνήγαγον θυσίαν τῷ εἰδώλῳ, καὶ εὐφραίνοντο ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai emoschopoiēsan en tais hēmerais ekeinais kai anēgagon thysian tō eidōlō, kai euphrainonto en tois ergois tōn cheirōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: But God turned, and gave them up to serve the host of heaven; as it is written in the book of the prophets, Did ye offer unto me slain beasts and sacrifices Forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
paragraphs.original: ἔστρεψεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς λατρεύειν τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῶν προφητῶν· Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ;
paragraphs.translit: estrepsen de ho theos kai paredōken autous latreuein tē stratia tou ouranou, kathōs gegraptai en biblō tōn prophētōn· Mē sphagia kai thysias prosēnenkate moi etē tesserakonta en tē erēmō, oikos Israēl;

paragraphs.text: And ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, And the star of the god Rephan, The figures which ye made to worship them: And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ Ῥαιφάν, τοὺς τύπους οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν αὐτοῖς. καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: kai anelabete tēn skēnēn tou Moloch kai to astron tou theou Rhaiphan, tous typous hous epoiēsate proskynein autois. kai metoikiō hymas epekeina Babylōnos.

paragraphs.text: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the testimony in the wilderness, even as he appointed who spake unto Moses, that he should make it according to the figure that he had seen.
paragraphs.original: Ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἦν τοῖς πατράσιν ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθὼς διετάξατο ὁ λαλῶν τῷ Μωϋσῇ ποιῆσαι αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸν τύπον ὃν ἑωράκει,
paragraphs.translit: Hē skēnē tou martyriou ēn tois patrasin hēmōn en tē erēmō, kathōs dietaxato ho lalōn tō Mōysē poiēsai autēn kata ton typon hon heōrakei,

paragraphs.text: Which also our fathers, in their turn, brought in with Joshua when they entered on the possession of the nations, that God thrust out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David;
paragraphs.original: ἣν καὶ εἰσήγαγον διαδεξάμενοι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ κατασχέσει τῶν ἐθνῶν ὧν ἐξῶσεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἕως τῶν ἡμερῶν Δαυίδ·
paragraphs.translit: hēn kai eisēgagon diadexamenoi hoi pateres hēmōn meta Iēsou en tē kataschesei tōn ethnōn hōn exōsen ho theos apo prosōpou tōn paterōn hēmōn heōs tōn hēmerōn Dauid·

paragraphs.text: who found favor in the sight of God, and asked to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.
paragraphs.original: ὃς εὗρεν χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ᾐτήσατο εὑρεῖν σκήνωμα τῷ θεῷ Ἰακώβ.
paragraphs.translit: hos heuren charin enōpion tou theou kai ētēsato heurein skēnōma tō theō Iakōb.

paragraphs.text: But Solomon built him a house.
paragraphs.original: Σολομῶν δὲ οἰκοδόμησεν αὐτῷ οἶκον.
paragraphs.translit: Solomōn de oikodomēsen autō oikon.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in [houses] made with hands; as saith the prophet,
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐχ ὁ ὕψιστος ἐν χειροποιήτοις κατοικεῖ· καθὼς ὁ προφήτης λέγει·
paragraphs.translit: allʼ ouch ho hypsistos en cheiropoiētois katoikei· kathōs ho prophētēs legei·

paragraphs.text: The heaven is my throne, And the earth the footstool of my feet: What manner of house will ye build me? saith the Lord: Or what is the place of my rest?
paragraphs.original: Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου· ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι, λέγει κύριος, ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου;
paragraphs.translit: Ho ouranos moi thronos, hē de gē hypopodion tōn podōn mou· poion oikon oikodomēsete moi, legei kyrios, ē tis topos tēs katapauseōs mou;

paragraphs.text: Did not my hand make all these things?
paragraphs.original: οὐχὶ ἡ χείρ μου ἐποίησεν ταῦτα πάντα;
paragraphs.translit: ouchi hē cheir mou epoiēsen tauta panta;

paragraphs.text: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Spirit: as your fathers did, so do ye.
paragraphs.original: Σκληροτράχηλοι καὶ ἀπερίτμητοι καρδίαις καὶ τοῖς ὠσίν, ὑμεῖς ἀεὶ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ ἀντιπίπτετε, ὡς οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ ὑμεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Sklērotrachēloi kai aperitmētoi kardiais kai tois ōsin, hymeis aei tō pneumati tō hagiō antipiptete, hōs hoi pateres hymōn kai hymeis.

paragraphs.text: Which of the prophets did not your fathers persecute? and they killed them that showed before of the coming of the Righteous One; of whom ye have now become betrayers and murderers;
paragraphs.original: τίνα τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἐδίωξαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν; καὶ ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς προκαταγγείλαντας περὶ τῆς ἐλεύσεως τοῦ δικαίου οὗ νῦν ὑμεῖς προδόται καὶ φονεῖς ἐγένεσθε,
paragraphs.translit: tina tōn prophētōn ouk ediōxan hoi pateres hymōn; kai apekteinan tous prokatangeilantas peri tēs eleuseōs tou dikaiou hou nyn hymeis prodotai kai phoneis egenesthe,

paragraphs.text: ye who received the law as it was ordained by angels, and kept it not.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες ἐλάβετε τὸν νόμον εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων, καὶ οὐκ ἐφυλάξατε.
paragraphs.translit: hoitines elabete ton nomon eis diatagas angelōn, kai ouk ephylaxate.

paragraphs.text: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούοντες δὲ ταῦτα διεπρίοντο ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν καὶ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Akouontes de tauta dieprionto tais kardiais autōn kai ebrychon tous odontas epʼ auton.

paragraphs.text: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,
paragraphs.original: ὑπάρχων δὲ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶδεν δόξαν θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: hyparchōn de plērēs pneumatos hagiou atenisas eis ton ouranon eiden doxan theou kai Iēsoun hestōta ek dexiōn tou theou,

paragraphs.text: and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing on the right hand of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ θεωρῶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς διηνοιγμένους καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν ἑστῶτα τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· Idou theōrō tous ouranous diēnoigmenous kai ton hyion tou anthrōpou ek dexiōn hestōta tou theou.

paragraphs.text: But they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and rushed upon him with one accord;
paragraphs.original: κράξαντες δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν, καὶ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπʼ αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: kraxantes de phōnē megalē syneschon ta ōta autōn, kai hōrmēsan homothymadon epʼ auton,

paragraphs.text: and they cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες ἔξω τῆς πόλεως ἐλιθοβόλουν. καὶ οἱ μάρτυρες ἀπέθεντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας νεανίου καλουμένου Σαύλου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekbalontes exō tēs poleōs elithoboloun. kai hoi martyres apethento ta himatia autōn para tous podas neaniou kaloumenou Saulou.

paragraphs.text: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon [the Lord], and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλιθοβόλουν τὸν Στέφανον ἐπικαλούμενον καὶ λέγοντα· Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου·
paragraphs.translit: kai elithoboloun ton Stephanon epikaloumenon kai legonta· Kyrie Iēsou, dexai to pneuma mou·

paragraphs.text: And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
paragraphs.original: θεὶς δὲ τὰ γόνατα ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Κύριε, μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν· καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐκοιμήθη.
paragraphs.translit: theis de ta gonata ekraxen phōnē megalē· Kyrie, mē stēsēs autois tautēn tēn hamartian· kai touto eipōn ekoimēthē.
